QASHANI:12:41-42/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:12:41-42/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:12:41-42/r1.claim: The cupbearer's fate means that attachment to pleasures is imposed on the spirit after restraint from association.
QASHANI:12:41-42/r1.anchor: تعيين لشأن الأول بعد السياسة بالمنع عن الشرك

QASHANI:12:41-42/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:12:41-42/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:12:41-42/r2.claim: The baker's crucifixion means suppressing desire and fixing it to vegetative nature so imagination and animal faculties cannot act through it; after desire dies, the soul's powers fulfill divine rights.
QASHANI:12:41-42/r2.anchor: منعه عن أفعاله بنفسه وقمعه عن مقتضاه وتثبيته وتقريره على جذع القوة الطبيعية

QASHANI:12:41-42/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:12:41-42/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:12:41-42/r3.claim: Their declared outcome marks Joseph's approach to God and the emergence of sainthood through annihilation in God.
QASHANI:12:41-42/r3.anchor: وقت وصوله وتقربه من الله وأوان ظهور مقام الولاية بالفناء في الله

QUSHAYRI:v2p77/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p77/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p77/r8.claim: The two prisoners shared a question and imprisonment but had opposite outcomes: one was executed and the other favored and elevated.
QUSHAYRI:v2p77/r8.anchor: وفي دخول السجن ، ولكن تباينا في المآل

QUSHAYRI:v2p77/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p77/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p77/r9.claim: Dream interpretation, even when true, proceeds by predominance of probability rather than certainty.
QUSHAYRI:v2p77/r9.anchor: فهو بطريق غلبة الظن دون القطع

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p335/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p335/r1.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p335/r1.claim: The referenced form may be a plural of عشوة, meaning darkness, with its separate portions motivating the plural.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p335/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون جمع عشوة: أي ظلاما، وجمعه لتفرق أجزائه

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p343/r5.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p343/r5.speaker: عكرمة والجحدري
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p343/r5.claim: ʿIkrimah and al-Jaḥdarī read فيسقى ربه خمرا, making the cupbearer's good outcome parallel to the other prisoner's punishment.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p343/r5.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة عكرمة والجحدري: "فيسقى ربه خمرا"3

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r4.claim: After delivering the more important teaching about religion, Joseph calls the men his prison companions again so they will focus on the interpretation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r4.anchor: لما ألقى إليهما ما كان أهم وهو أمر الدين رجاء في إيمانهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r5.claim: Joseph tells Bunū that he will return to his former post serving the king; three vine branches mean three more days in prison before release.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r5.anchor: فروي أنه قال: لبنو: أما أنت فتعود إلى مرتبتك وسقاية ربك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r6.claim: Joseph tells Malḥab that his three baskets mean three days until he is released and crucified.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r6.anchor: وقال لملحب: أما أنت فما رأيت من السلال ثلاثة أيام ثم تخرج فتصلب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r7.claim: Some reports say the men denied seeing anything because they had pretended to test Joseph; another says only the man told he would be crucified said this, while another says both saw and then denied it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r7.anchor: فروي أنهما قالا: ما رأينا شيئا، وإنما تحالمنا لنجربك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r8.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r8.claim: The majority read yasqī from saqā; another group reads yusqī from asqā, and both verbs can mean the same thing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: فيسقي ربه من سقى، وفرقة: فيسقي من أسقى، وهما لغتان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r9.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r9.claim: The Lawāmiʿ author says saqā and asqā are synonyms, though the usual distinction is giving a drink versus providing water.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r9.anchor: وقال صاحب اللوامح: سقى وأسقى بمعنى واحد في اللغة، والمعروف أن سقاه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r10.speaker: عكرمة والجحدري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r10.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Jaḥdarī read the passive yusqā, meaning that the king will be given wine to drink.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r11.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya understands ربه as the prisoner's master.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r12.claim: Joseph tells the prisoners through knowledge from God that the outcome is decreed whether their dreams were genuine or feigned.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r12.anchor: ثم أخبرهما يوسف عليه السلام عن غيب علمه من قبل الله أن الأمر قد قضي ووافق القدر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r13.claim: The singular الأمر refers to the final outcome of the accusation that jailed the men: one is saved and one killed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p278/r13.anchor: وأفرد الأمر وإن كان أمر هذا، لأن المقصود إنما هو عاقبة أمرهما

ALUSI-FULL:v12p245#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p245#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p245#2/r1.claim: After proving his knowledge, Joseph resumes the answer with a repeated address because interpretation is a new topic; he means the cupbearer without naming him, trusting the interpretation and observing good companionship.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p245#2/r1.anchor: بعد تحقيق الحق وبيانه لهما مقدار علمه الواسع شرع في إنبائهما

ALUSI-FULL:v12p245#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p245#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p245#2/r2.claim: Joseph interprets the cupbearer’s vine as the king and restored favor; three branches mean three days until release and return to service. The baker’s three baskets mean three days until release and crucifixion, with birds eating his head.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p245#2/r2.anchor: روي أنه عليه السلام قال له : ما رأيت من الكرمة وحسنها هو الملك

ALUSI-FULL:v12p245#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p245#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p245#2/r3.claim: A reading has yusqā passive; another uses active asqā. Saqā and asqā can both mean giving drink, though convention distinguishes giving a drink from providing watering; ʿIkrima is also reported to read passively with riyyihi as second object.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p245#2/r3.anchor: وقريء ( فيسقى ) بضم الياء والبناء للفاعل من أسقى

ALUSI-FULL:v12p245#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p245#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p245#2/r4.claim: Quḍiya means completed or settled: the matter the two men asked about has been decided.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p245#2/r4.anchor: قضي ( أتم وأحكم ( الأمر الذي فيه تستفتيان

ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r1.claim: The prisoners' visions foreshadow one man's rescue and the other's destruction; their questioning asks for the visions' interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r1.anchor: نجاة أحدكما وهلاك الآخر ومعنى استفتائهما فيه سؤالهما عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r2.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the two prisoners feigned dreams to test Joseph; after he interpreted them, they said they had been playing and had seen nothing.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r2.anchor: ما رأى صاحبا يوسف شيئا إنما تحالما ليجربا علمه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r3.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r3.claim: An unnamed investigator says the settled matter is the dreams themselves, not the men's eventual fates, because an inquiry seeks an answer about an incident, not its outcome.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r3.anchor: ذهب بعض المحققين إلى أن المراد به ما رأياه من الرؤيتين ونفى أن يكون المراد ما يؤول إليه أمرهما

ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r4.claim: The investigator argues that asking for interpretation means asking about the dreams as events, analogizing the king's request to be advised about his dream.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r4.anchor: لأن الإستفتاء إنما يكون في الحادثة لا في حكمها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r5.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r5.claim: He reads the wording as magnifying the dreams: the text calls them an affair and their request an inquiry because such inquiry concerns obscure, momentous cases; the present tense prolongs the request until Joseph finishes answering.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r5.anchor: وعبر عن ذلك بالأمر وعن طلب تأويله بالإستفتاء تهويلا لأمره وتفخيما لشأنه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r6.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r6.claim: He explains the singular 'matter' despite two dreams as matching the prisoners' own singular wording, and says they asked about the image of the outcome rather than their crime or its cause.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r6.anchor: على حسب ما وحداه في قولهما

ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r7.claim: Al-Alusi objects that the investigator's distinction between the matter and the event is inconsistent: if the outcome and dream are treated as identical for predication, they can also be identical for inquiry.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r7.anchor: بعد اعتبار العينية بين شيئين يكون صحة نسبة ما هو من أحوال أحدهما إلى الآخر

ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r8.speaker: الكثير
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r8.claim: Many exegetes take the matter as the men's eventual outcome and understand the preposition causally: they asked about the dreams in order to learn their fate; Al-Alusi finds this the stronger, less strained reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r8.anchor: ويرجح ما ذهب إليه الكثير أن فيه سلامة من نزع الخف قبل الوصول إلى الماء

ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r9.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r9.claim: Another view takes the matter as the crime for which the men were accused and imprisoned, supplying an omitted noun meaning the consequence of that accusation.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r9.anchor: المراد بالأمر ما اتهما به والكلام حينئذ على حذف مضاف

ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r10.claim: The report of Joseph's answer may be a rebuttal to the prisoners' denial or a confirmation of his interpretation; a lie by the cupbearer could have protected his companion, and another report says the baker was the one who denied it.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r10.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون للرد عليهما حسبما ورد في الأثر يحتمل أن يكون تحقيقا لتعبيره

ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r11.claim: The episode is cited for the maxim that dreams occur as first interpreted, expressed in the saying that a dream rests on a bird's wing until told, then falls.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p246/r11.anchor: المنام على جناح طائر إذا قص وقع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p243#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p243#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p243#2/r1.claim: The cupbearer will serve wine to his master, the king; after three days he will be released and restored to his former position.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p243#2/r1.anchor: {يا صاحبي السجن أما أحدكما} وهو صاحب الشراب، {فيسقي ربه} [يعني الملك] (2) {خمرا}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p243#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p243#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p243#2/r2.claim: The baker will be released after three days only to be crucified, so birds eat from his head.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p243#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p243#2/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p243#2/r3.claim: Ibn Masud says both men admitted they had invented the dreams and were only playing; Joseph answered that God’s decree was settled regardless.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p243#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن مسعود: لما سمعا قول يوسف قالا ما رأينا شيئا إنما كنا نلعب، قال يوسف: {قضي الأمر الذي فيه تستفتيان}

NAHHAS:v2p329/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p329/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p329/r3.claim: Most linguists distinguish giving a drink from providing water; the Qur'anic form supports the latter despite a poem claiming synonymy.
NAHHAS:v2p329/r3.anchor: الذي عليه أكثر أهل اللغة أن معنى سقاه ناوله فشرب أو صب الماء

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:41/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:41/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:41/r1.claim: The cupbearer will return to serving his master wine, while the baker will be crucified and birds will eat from his head.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:41/r1.anchor: { يصاحبي السجن أما أحدكما } يعني الشرابي. { فيسقي ربه خمرا } كما كان يسقيه قبل

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:41/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:41/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:41/r2.claim: The two men said Joseph had lied, and he replied that the matter they asked about was settled; it is singular because they sought to learn the shared outcome of their cases.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:41/r2.anchor: { قضى الأمر الذي فيه تستفتيان } أي قطع الأمر الذي تستفتيان فيه، وهو ما يؤول إليه أمركما

BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r1.claim: Calling them prison companions evokes shared hardship, which removes worldly pretension and softens the heart toward friendship.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r1.anchor: أي الذي تزول فيه الحظوظ ويحصل الانكسار للنفس والرقة في القلب فتتخلص فيه المودة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r2.claim: Joseph leaves the identity of the condemned prisoner ambiguous, allowing each man to hope he is the one restored unless they demand a specific answer.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r2.anchor: فإن ألجأه إلى التعيين كان ذلك عذرا له في الخروج عن الأليق

BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r3.claim: The cupbearer will serve wine to his master again; the baker will be crucified by the king and birds will eat from his head.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r3.anchor: وهو الساقي فيلخص ويقرب { فيسقي ربه } أي سيده الذي في خدمته

BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r4.claim: The passive verb for crucifixion reflects that only the king has authority to crucify; the paired clauses use ellipsis, with each outcome implying its opposite counterpart.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r5.claim: A report says the two men denied seeing anything and said they were playing, but Joseph insists their case is settled and his interpretation is neither ignorance nor error.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r5.anchor: وروى أنهما قالا : ما رأينا شيئا , إنما كنا نلعب

BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r6.speaker: الرماني
BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r6.claim: Al-Rummani distinguishes fatwa as an answer about a matter's meaning from an answer that gives its underlying cause.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r6.anchor: الجواب بحكم المعنى , وهو غير الجواب بعلته - ذكره الرماني

BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r7.claim: The dreams may foreshadow the king's: pressed grapes signify green ears and fat cattle, while the birds eating the baker's bread signify dry ears and lean cattle.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p43/r7.anchor: فالعصير يشير إلى السنابل الخضر والبقر السمان

DURR-FULL:v4p536/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p536/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v4p536/r1.claim: Joseph predicted that Mujlab would be crucified and birds would eat from his head, while Nabwa would return to his post and regain his master's favor.
DURR-FULL:v4p536/r1.anchor: ثم قال لمجلب: أما أنت فتصلب فتأكل الطير من رأسك

DURR-FULL:v4p538/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p538/r8.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v4p538/r8.claim: Ikrima describes the cupbearer's dream as planting a grape seed that grew clusters, pressing them, and serving the king; Joseph predicted three more prison days before his return to service.
DURR-FULL:v4p538/r8.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه قال: أتاه فقال: رأيت فيما يرى النائم أني غرست حبة من عنب

DURR-FULL:v4p538/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p538/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v4p538/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd says the cupbearer would serve his master, explaining rabbahu as his lord or master.
DURR-FULL:v4p538/r9.anchor: عن ابن زيد رضي الله عنه في قوله {فيسقي ربه خمرا} قال: سيده

DURR-FULL:v4p538/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p538/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v4p538/r10.claim: Ibn Masud says the prisoners invented the dreams to test Joseph; after he interpreted them they claimed to have been playing, but the interpretation had already fixed the outcome.
DURR-FULL:v4p538/r10.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: ما رأى صاحبا سجن يوسف عليه السلام شيئا إنما تحاكما إليه

DURR-FULL:v4p540/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p540/r1.speaker: أبو مجلز
DURR-FULL:v4p540/r1.claim: Abu Majliz says one of the two prisoners who described a dream to Joseph was lying.
DURR-FULL:v4p540/r1.anchor: عن أبي مجلز رضي الله عنه قال: كان أحد اللذين قصا على يوسف الرؤيا كاذبا

DURR-FULL:v4p540/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p540/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p540/r2.claim: Mujahid says the decision was fixed when the prisoners claimed they had made up the dreams: their real dreams had taken effect as Joseph interpreted them.
DURR-FULL:v4p540/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {قضي الأمر الذي فيه تستفتيان} قال عند قولهما

DURR-FULL:v4p540/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p540/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p540/r3.claim: Qatadah identifies the doomed man as the baker and the restored man as the cupbearer; both denied having dreamed, but Joseph's prediction stood.
DURR-FULL:v4p540/r3.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه قال: قال يوسف عليه السلام للخباز: إنك تصلب فتأكل الطير من رأسك

DURR-FULL:v4p540/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p540/r4.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v4p540/r4.claim: Ikrima recited the clause with the wording أما أحدكما فيسقي ربه خمرا.
DURR-FULL:v4p540/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه أنه قرأ {أما أحدكما فيسقي ربه خمرا}

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2147/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2147/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2147/r1.claim: Joseph told Majlath he would be crucified and birds would eat from his head, while Nabū would return to his post and regain his master's favor.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2147/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ثم قال لمجلث : اما انت فتصلب فتاكل الطير من راسك ، وقال لنبو : اما انت فترد على عملك

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2147/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2147/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2147/r2.claim: A report attributed to Muhammad ibn Abbas says Joseph delayed interpretation because it foretold execution; the royal meal was sent to a prisoner intended for death, and Joseph first spoke of food to prompt their repeated request.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2147/r2.anchor: ثنا ابن جريج لا ياتيكما طعام ترزقانه زعم محمد بن عباس ، قال : كره العبارة لهما ، فغدا ، فقال : لا ياتيكما طعام

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2147/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2147/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2147/r3.claim: The prisoners panicked at the interpretations and said they had seen nothing; Joseph replied that the matter they asked about had been decided.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2147/r3.anchor: عن السدي : يا صاحبي السجن اما احدكما فيسقي ربه خمرا فيعاد على مكانه واما الاخر فيصلب فتاكل الطير من راسه

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2147/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2147/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2147/r4.claim: When the prisoners said they had seen nothing, Joseph's “the matter is decided” meant that the interpretation had occurred.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2147/r4.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة ، عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال : لما قصا على يوسف ، فاخبرهما قالا : انا لم نر شيئا ، قال : قضي الامر الذي فيه تستفتيان

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2147/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2147/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2147/r5.claim: The two prisoners had lied to test Joseph; after his interpretation they said they had only been playing, but he said the decision was already made.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2147/r5.anchor: عن إبراهيم ، عن علقمة ، عن عبد الله ، انه قال في الفتيين الذين اتيا يوسف في الرؤيا : انما كذبا ليجرباه

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2148/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2148/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2148/r1.claim: Joseph says the matter they had asked about was inevitable.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2148/r1.anchor: عن السدي قال يوسف : قضي الامر الذي فيه تستفتيان ان هذا كائن لا بد منه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p277/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p277/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p277/r1.claim: Joseph's vocative stresses the importance of his interpretation and addresses them as fellow prisoners.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p277/r1.anchor: افتتح خطابهما بالنداء اهتماما بما يلقيه إليهما من التعبير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p277/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p277/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p277/r2.claim: If Joseph spoke in the order shown, he gave both interpretations together in a veiled summary so the condemned man could work out his fate gradually.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p277/r2.anchor: في عبارة واحدة مجملة ، لأن في تأويل إحدى الرؤيين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p277/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p277/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p277/r3.claim: Alternatively, the verse may condense Joseph's original speech, in which he directly assigned each interpretation to one man.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p277/r3.anchor: كان في الآية إيجاز لحكاية كلام يوسف عليه السلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p277/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p277/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p277/r4.claim: “The matter is decided” confirms the interpretation because their urgent question concerned what would happen to them in prison.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p277/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p277/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p277/r5.claim: Istiftāʾ is asking for a fatwa: an explanation that resolves difficulty or uncertainty; the verb aftā retains its hamza and is linked by some to fatā, youth, because clear explanation strengthens the recipient.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p277/r5.anchor: الإخبار بإزالة مشكل ، أو إرشاد إلى إزالة حيرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r5.claim: Joseph reportedly told Banu he would return to his former position serving the king, and Majlath would be crucified, after three days.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r5.anchor: أما أنت فتعود إلى مرتبتك وسقاية ربك، وقال لمجلث

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r6.claim: One report says both prisoners denied having seen dreams and said they had invented them to test Joseph; another says only the man sentenced to crucifixion denied it, while a third says they saw them but later denied it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r6.anchor: ما رأينا شيئا وإنما تحالمنا لنجربك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r7.claim: Some read يسقي from saqā and others from asqā, two verbs with the same meaning; ʿIkrima and al-Jaḥdari read the passive form, meaning he will be given wine to drink.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r7.anchor: بضم الياء وفتح القاف أي ما يرويه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r8.claim: Joseph reports knowledge of the unseen granted by God and says the matter has already been decreed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p246/r8.anchor: عن غيب علمه من قبل الله تعالى: إن الأمر قد قضي

SAMIN-DURR:12:41/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:41/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:12:41/r1.claim: The common reading فيسقي has an open yāʾ from سقاه يسقيه; عكرمة reads a damma from أسقى, a synonymous verb, also seen in the readings of 56:69.
SAMIN-DURR:12:41/r1.anchor: العامة على فتح الياء، من سقاه يسقيه. وقرأ عكرمة في رواية " فيسقي " بضم حرف المضارعة

SAMIN-DURR:12:41/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:41/r2.speaker: عكرمة والجحدري
SAMIN-DURR:12:41/r2.claim: They also read فيسقى ربه in the passive, with ربه nominative; al-Zamakhshari attributes this only to عكرمة.
SAMIN-DURR:12:41/r2.anchor: ونقل ابن عطية عن عكرمة والجحدري أنهما قرآ " فيسقى ربه " مبنيا للمفعول ورفع " ربه ".

SAMIN-DURR:12:41/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:41/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:12:41/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari asks why قضي الأمر is singular when the two men asked about different outcomes, and answers that it means the matter for which they were accused and imprisoned.
SAMIN-DURR:12:41/r3.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " ما استفتيا في أمر واحد. بل في أمرين مختلفين، فما وجه التوحيد؟

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p226#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p226#2/r1.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p226#2/r1.claim: Ibn al-Sa'ib says rabb here means master; Joseph predicts that the cupbearer will serve wine to his master after three days and regain his old position.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p226#2/r1.anchor: الرب هاهنا السيد قال ابن السائب لما قص الساقي رؤياه على يوسف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p226#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p226#2/r2.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p226#2/r2.claim: Ibn al-Sa'ib says Joseph tells the baker that in three days the king will execute and crucify him, and birds will eat from his head.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p226#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p226#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p226#2/r3.claim: “The matter is decided” means the interpretation has been settled, whether the prisoners' dreams were true or false.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p226#2/r3.anchor: أي فرغ منه وسبقع بكما صدقتما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p226#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p226#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p226#2/r4.claim: One answer to why Joseph was certain is that revelation told him; the declaration that the matter was decided shows it was revealed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p226#2/r4.anchor: أنه حتم ذلك لوحي أتاه من الله وسبيل المنام المكذوب فيه أن لا يقع تأويله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p226#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p226#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p226#2/r5.claim: The alternative says he did not guarantee the events: “the matter is decided” may mean only that he has finished answering their question.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p226#2/r5.anchor: أنه لم يحتم بدليل قوله وقال للذي ظن أنه ناج منهما

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p390/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p390/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p390/r1.claim: Yusuf leaves the cupbearer's identity unstated to spare the other prisoner, though the first will serve his master and the other will be crucified and eaten by birds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p390/r1.anchor: وهو الذي رأى أنه يعصر خمرا، ولكنه لم يعينه لئلا يحزن ذاك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p390/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p390/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p390/r2.claim: Yusuf says the matter is settled because a dream remains suspended until interpreted and then comes to pass.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p390/r2.anchor: لأن الرؤيا على رجل طائر ما لم تعبر، فإذا عبرت وقعت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p390/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p390/r3.speaker: عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p390/r3.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the prisoners then denied having seen anything, prompting Yusuf to say their question was settled; Mujahid and others give the same explanation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p390/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: لما قالا ما قالا وأخبرهما، قالا ما رأينا شيئا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p390/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p390/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p390/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir generalizes that whoever invents a dream and receives an interpretation is bound by that interpretation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p390/r4.anchor: أن من تحلم بباطل وفسره، فإنه يلزم بتأويله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p390/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p390/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p390/r5.claim: Ahmad transmits from Muawiya ibn Hayda the Prophetic report that a dream is suspended until interpreted, after which it occurs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p390/r5.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "الرؤيا على رجل طائر ما لم تعبر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p390/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p390/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p390/r6.claim: A report in Abu Ya'la's Musnad, through Anas, says a dream follows the first interpreter.

JISHUMI:v5p3646/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3646/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3646/r5.claim: Qaḍā means completing and executing something fully; hence لما قضي means when it was finished, and a qāḍī is so named.
JISHUMI:v5p3646/r5.anchor: وقضاء الشيء: إحكامه وإمضاؤه، والفراغ منه على التمام، ومنه: (لما قضي)

JISHUMI:v5p3646/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3646/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3646/r6.claim: Istiftāʾ is asking for a legal opinion; fatwā answers the legal question itself, not the reasoning behind it.
JISHUMI:v5p3646/r6.anchor: والاستفتاء: طلب الفتيا، وهو استفعال منه، والفتيا: جواب حكم المعنى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p444#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p444#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p444#3/r1.claim: The one who will serve wine is the cupbearer; one reading has him give his lord a drink, while ʿIkrima's reading uses a passive construction.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p444#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p444#3/r2.speaker: عكرمة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p444#3/r2.claim: ʿIkrima reads yusqā rabbahu, with the passive meaning that he will be given drink to satisfy him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p444#3/r2.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة ( فيسقي ربه ) أي يسقي ما يروي به على البناء للمفعول

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p444#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p444#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p444#3/r3.claim: Yusuf interprets the cupbearer's vine as the king and his good standing, with three days in prison before release; the baker's three baskets mean three days before execution.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p444#3/r3.anchor: ثم تخرج وتعود إلى ما كنت عليه ، وقال للثاني : ما رأيت من السلال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p444#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p444#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p444#3/r4.claim: Although the men asked about different dreams, al-amr means their shared accusation of poisoning and the outcome of their imprisonment: one would escape and one die.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p444#3/r4.anchor: المراد بالأمر ما اتهما به من سم الملك وما سجنا من أجله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p444#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p444#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p444#3/r5.claim: Alternatively, the men had fabricated the dreams to test Yusuf; he told them the outcome would occur whether they had spoken truthfully or lied.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p444#3/r5.anchor: وقيل : جحدا وقالا : ما رأينا شيئا ، على ما روي أنهما تحالما له

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r1.claim: The cupbearer, whose dream concerned pressing grapes, will survive and resume serving wine to his master.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r1.anchor: وهو الذي قال : إني أراني أعصر خمرا , بشره بالنجاة وعوده إلى سقي سيده خمرا

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r2.claim: The baker, whose dream showed birds eating from bread on his head, will be killed by crucifixion; he was the king's baker.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r2.anchor: وهو الذي قال { إني أراني أحمل فوق رأسي خبزا تأكل الطير منه } فأنذره بالهلكة وكان خباز الملك

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r3.speaker: ابن جرير
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r3.claim: Ibn Jarir names the baker Majlatha and the cupbearer Nabwa.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن جرير : وكان اسمه مجلثا , واسم الساقي نبوا

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r4.claim: After hearing the doomed prisoner's dream interpretation, he protested that they had only been playing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r4.anchor: فلما سمع الهالك منهما تأويل رؤياه قال : إنما كنا نلعب

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r5.claim: The decree means either that the question and answer are finished or that its interpretation will soon be fulfilled.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r5.anchor: فيه وجهان : أحدهما : قضي السؤال والجواب . الثاني : سيقضى تأويله ويقع

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r6.claim: Joseph's certainty about the interpretation may have come from revelation from God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r6.anchor: يجوز أن يكون قاله عن وحي من الله تعالى

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r7.claim: Alternatively, as a prophet, Joseph could be certain of what God caused him to say, unlike a nonprophet.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p38#2/r7.anchor: لأنه نبي يقطع بتحقيق ما أنطقه الله تعالى وأجراه على لسانه , بخلاف من ليس بنبي

MUQATIL:12:41-42/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:41-42/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:41-42/r1.claim: Joseph predicts that the cupbearer will leave prison in three days, return to his work, and serve his master wine; the baker will be executed and eaten by birds.
MUQATIL:12:41-42/r1.anchor: { يصاحبي السجن أمآ أحدكما فيسقي ربه خمرا } ، وهو الساقي، قال له يوسف: تكون في السجن ثلاثة أيام، ثم تخرج فتكون على عملك،

MUQATIL:12:41-42/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:41-42/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:41-42/r2.claim: When the baker tried to deny the dream, Joseph said the outcome was settled whether or not they had truly dreamed it.
MUQATIL:12:41-42/r2.anchor: فكره الخباز تعبير رؤياه، فقال: ما رأيت شيئا، إنما كنت ألعب، فقال له يوسف: { قضي الأمر الذي فيه تستفتيان }

NASAFI-FULL:v2p190/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190/r1.claim: The cupbearer will return to serving his master wine and resume his former work; the baker will be crucified and birds will eat from his head.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190/r1.anchor: يريد الشرابى ﴿ فيسقي ربه ﴾ سيده ﴿ خمرا ﴾ أى يعود إلى عمله

NASAFI-FULL:v2p190/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190/r2.claim: Joseph interprets three vine branches as three days in prison, after which the cupbearer returns to his former station; three baskets mean the baker will be killed after three days.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190/r2.anchor: ما رأيت من الكرمة وحسنها هو الملك وحسن حالك عنده

NASAFI-FULL:v2p190/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190/r3.claim: When the baker denied having seen anything after hearing the interpretation, Joseph said that the matter being asked about was settled: one would perish and the other escape.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190/r3.anchor: أى قطع وتم ما تستفتيان فيه من أمركما وشأنكما

ZAJJAJ:v3p110/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p110/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p110/r4.claim: The cupbearer is the one who will serve wine to his master, the king. Sāqā means to hand someone a drink, while asqā means to provide water or irrigation.
ZAJJAJ:v3p110/r4.anchor: فكان هذا صاحب شراب الملك، فأعلمه أن تأويل ما رأى هو هذا

ZAJJAJ:v3p111/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p111/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p111/r1.claim: When the condemned man denied having seen a dream, Joseph told him the predicted crucifixion would still happen, just as he knew what food would arrive.
ZAJJAJ:v3p111/r1.anchor: قال الذي أنبأه بأنه يصلب أنه لم ير شيئا فأعلمه أن ذلك واقع به وإن لم ير

QURTUBI-FULL:12:41/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:41/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:41/r1.claim: Joseph told the cupbearer he would return to serving the king after three days, while the other man would be crucified after three days and eaten by birds; whether dreamed or not, the decree was settled.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:41/r1.anchor: قال للساقي: إنك ترد على عملك الذي كنت عليه من سقي الملك بعد ثلاثة أيام

QURTUBI-FULL:12:41/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:41/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:41/r2.claim: Some linguists use سقى and أسقى synonymously; al-Nahhas says most distinguish giving someone water to drink from providing a source of water.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:41/r2.anchor:
وحكى أهل اللغة أن سقى وأسقى لغتان بمعنى واحد، كما قال الشاعر:
سقى قومي بني

QURTUBI-FULL:12:41/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:41/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:41/r3.claim: A false dream interpretation does not bind someone; Joseph's interpretation became a decree because he was a prophet and God made it occur to confirm his prophethood.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:41/r3.anchor: لا يلزمه وإنما كان ذلك في يوسف لأنه نبي، وتعبير النبي حكم، وقد قال: إنه

QURTUBI-FULL:12:41/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:41/r4.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:12:41/r4.claim: A report from Qatada says a man told Umar he dreamed of alternating lush growth and drought; Umar predicted alternating faith and apostasy ending in death as an unbeliever, and the man said he had dreamed nothing.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:41/r4.anchor: فقد روى عبد الرزاق عن معمر عن قتادة قال: جاء رجل إلى عمر بن الخطاب

QURTUBI-FULL:12:41/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:41/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:41/r5.claim: The author says this sort of prediction was exceptional for Umar, a divinely inspired man whose intuitions and statements came true, citing two further examples.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:41/r5.anchor: قلنا: ليست لأحد بعد عمر لأن عمر كان محدثا، وكان إذا ظن ظنا كان وإذا

RAZI-FULL:v18p107/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p107/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p107/r7.claim: Joseph could infer that they served the king from their use of rabb for their master in the later statements about serving wine and asking to be remembered.
RAZI-FULL:v18p107/r7.anchor: هما غلامان كانا للملك الأكبر بمصر أحدهما صاحب طعامه

RAZI-FULL:v18p114#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p114#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p114#2/r1.claim: Joseph interprets the cupbearer's vine as a return to service after three days, and the baker's three baskets as execution and birds eating from his head.
RAZI-FULL:v18p114#2/r1.anchor: أما حسن العنبة فهو حسن حالك

RAZI-FULL:v18p114#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p114#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p114#2/r2.claim: The two men later said they had seen nothing; one view is that they invented the dreams to test Joseph, while another says they disliked his answer.
RAZI-FULL:v18p114#2/r2.anchor: واختلف فيما لأجله قالا ما رأينا شيئا فقيل إنهما وضعا هذا الكلام ليختبرا علمه

RAZI-FULL:v18p114#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p114#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v18p114#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says Joseph gave the interpretation rather than revelation; the verse's description of expectation as ظن also argues against certainty from revelation.
RAZI-FULL:v18p114#2/r3.anchor: لأن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما نقل أنه إنما ذكره على سبيل التعبير

RAZI-FULL:v18p114#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p114#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p114#2/r4.claim: He considers revelation possible: God may have disclosed each man's outcome when asked, though it appeared as dream interpretation; alternatively, Joseph's interpretive judgment need not mean an inevitable outcome.
RAZI-FULL:v18p114#2/r4.anchor: فلما نزل الوحي بذلك الغيب عند ذلك السؤال وقع في الظن أنه ذكره على سبيل التعبير

ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.claim: Unlike Genesis' romantic account of Joseph's fortunes, the Qur'anic story illustrates God's unfathomable direction of human affairs: people may hate what is good for them or love what is bad for them.
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.anchor: the Qur'an uses it primarily as an illustration of God's unfathomable direction of men's affairs

STUDYQURAN:12:41/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:41/r1.speaker: N and Kl
STUDYQURAN:12:41/r1.claim: The wine carrier would survive and regain his former post serving wine to Egypt’s king.
STUDYQURAN:12:41/r1.anchor: former position (N) as a wine server to the king of Egypt (Kl;

STUDYQURAN:12:41/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:41/r2.speaker: My
STUDYQURAN:12:41/r2.claim: The baker would be crucified for his crime, and birds would eat from his head after death.
STUDYQURAN:12:41/r2.anchor: the baker would be crucified for his crime, and after his death the birds would eat from his head (My;

TAB-FULL:v13p167/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p167/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p167/r1.claim: The one who serves his master wine is the dreamer who saw himself pressing wine; the other, whose bread birds eat, will be crucified and birds will eat from his head.
TAB-FULL:v13p167/r1.anchor: فيسقي ربه: يعني سيده وهو ملكهم، خمرا: يقول: يكون صاحب شرابه

TAB-FULL:v13p167/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p167/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p167/r2.claim: Rabb here means master or king; qadiya al-amr means the matter being asked about is finished and God's decree upon them has taken effect.
TAB-FULL:v13p167/r2.anchor: يقول: فرغ من الأمر الذي فيه استفتيتما، ووجب حكم الله عليكما بالذي أخبرتكما به

TAB-FULL:v13p167/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p167/r3.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v13p167/r3.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the two youths denied having seen dreams after Yusuf interpreted them, but Yusuf said the matter was already decided.
TAB-FULL:v13p167/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله، قال: " قال اللذان دخلا السجن على يوسف: ما رأينا شيئا فقال: {قضي الأمر الذي فيه تستفتيان} [يوسف: 41]

TAB-FULL:v13p169/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p169/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v13p169/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq identifies Mujlith as the one crucified and Nabu as the one restored to his former service and accepted by his master.
TAB-FULL:v13p169/r1.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: " قال لمجلث: أما أنت فتصلب فتأكل الطير من رأسك، وقال لنبو: أما أنت فترد على عملك

TAB-FULL:v13p169/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p169/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v13p169/r2.claim: Mujahid says the prediction had taken effect exactly as Yusuf interpreted when the youths claimed they had only been playing.
TAB-FULL:v13p169/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: " {قضي الأمر الذي فيه تستفتيان} [يوسف: 41] عند قولهما: ما رأينا رؤيا إنما كنا نلعب

TAB-FULL:v13p169/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p169/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v13p169/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj quotes the phrase 'in which you seek a decision' without adding a further gloss.

TABATABAI:12:40-41#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:40-41#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:40-41#2/r6.claim: The two predictions in this verse interpret the two prisoners’ dreams respectively: the cupbearer’s dream of pressing wine and the other prisoner’s dream of birds eating from his head.
TABATABAI:12:40-41#2/r6.anchor: معنى الآية ظاهر، وقرينة المناسبة قاضية

TABATABAI:12:41-42/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:41-42/r1.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام
TABATABAI:12:41-42/r1.claim: An Imami report says the second prisoner admitted that he had invented his dream after hearing that he would be crucified; Joseph replied that the matter he had asked about was already decreed.
TABATABAI:12:41-42/r1.anchor: ما ورد من الرواية من طرق أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام أن الثاني من الصاحبين قال له إني كذبت

TABATABAI:12:41-42/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:41-42/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:41-42/r4.claim: The view that Joseph interpreted the dreams only by conjecture conflicts with his declaration that the matter was settled and God’s statement that He taught him interpretation.
TABATABAI:12:41-42/r4.anchor: أنه صرح لهما بعلمه في قوله

TABATABAI:12:41-42#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:41-42#2/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:12:41-42#2/r2.claim: The same report identifies the two young men as the king’s servants, a baker and a cupbearer, and says the baker had fabricated the dream and was the one crucified.
TABATABAI:12:41-42#2/r2.anchor: ودخل معه السجن فتيان يقول عبدان للملك أحدهما خباز والآخر صاحب الشراب

TABRISI:12:39-41/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:39-41/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:39-41/r8.claim: The cupbearer's three grape clusters meant three more days in prison, then release on the fourth day and restoration to his post; Yusuf calls his master 'lord' as one says lord of a house or estate.
TABRISI:12:39-41/r8.anchor: أما العناقيد الثلاثة فإنها ثلاثة أيام تبقى في السجن

TABRISI:12:39-41/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:39-41/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:39-41/r9.claim: The other prisoner's baskets meant three more days before he was crucified and birds ate from his head; Yusuf's certain forecast shows he spoke by revelation of the unseen, not ordinary interpretation.
TABRISI:12:39-41/r9.anchor: أما السلال الثلاث فإنها ثلاثة أيام تبقى في السجن ثم يخرجك الملك فيصلبك

THALABI:v5p224/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p224/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
THALABI:v5p224/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿud says the two prisoners admitted they had seen nothing and were only testing Joseph; Joseph replied that the matter had already been decreed.
THALABI:v5p224/r1.anchor: قال ابن مسعود: لما سمعا قول يوسف قالا: ما رأينا شيئا إنما كنا نلعب

THALABI:v5p224/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p224/r2.speaker: أبو رزين العقيلي
THALABI:v5p224/r2.claim: Abu Ruzayn transmits the Prophet’s saying that a dream remains suspended until interpreted, is one forty-sixth of prophecy, and should be shared only with a person of judgment.
THALABI:v5p224/r2.anchor: قال: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: «إن الرؤيا على رجل طائر ما لم تعبر

THALABI:v5p224/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p224/r3.speaker: أنس
THALABI:v5p224/r3.claim: Anas transmits a prophetic report that a dream is realized according to its first interpreter.
THALABI:v5p224/r3.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «الرؤيا لأول عابرة»

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r1.claim: The cupbearer's dream showed a vine with three branches and grapes that he pressed for the king; Joseph predicted his return to service after three days.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي عن ابن عباس (¬3): لما قص الساقي رؤياه على يوسف وقد ذكرنا كيف قص عليه في موضعه، قال له يوسف: ما أحسن ما رأيت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r2.claim: Joseph told the baker that his three baskets foretold execution by the king after three days, with birds eating from his head.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r2.anchor: وقال للخباز لما قص عليه: بئس ما رأيت، السلال الثلاث، ثلاثة أيام يوجه إليك الملك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r3.claim: Joseph's firm prediction that the dreams would occur came from revelation; the fact that both men had fabricated their dreams yet the interpretations came true shows this.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r3.anchor: والجواب عن هذا: أن حكم (¬4) يوسف حتم بوقوع الأمر بهما من قبل وحي أتاه بذلك من الله تعالى،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd, Qatāda, and others say “the matter is decided” only ends the requested interpretation, not a certain prediction.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬1) وابن مسعود (¬2) وقتادة (¬3) وغيرهم (¬4)، قالوا: لما عبر رؤياهما، قالا ما رأينا شيئا،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd agrees that يوسف's words finish the interpretation requested by the prisoners without guaranteeing its fulfillment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬1) وابن مسعود (¬2) وقتادة (¬3) وغيرهم (¬4)، قالوا: لما عبر رؤياهما،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r6.claim: Qatāda agrees that يوسف's words finish the interpretation requested by the prisoners without guaranteeing its fulfillment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬1) وابن مسعود (¬2) وقتادة (¬3) وغيرهم (¬4)، قالوا: لما عبر رؤياهما،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r7.claim: Al-Wāḥidī prefers the revelation-based certainty reading as more fitting to a prophet's state.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r7.anchor: والصحيح هو الأول؛ لأنه أشبه بحال الأنبياء (¬5)،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r8.claim: The word الاستفتاء was explained earlier in the commentary on al-Nisāʾ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p120#2/r8.anchor: وذكرنا معنى الاستفتاء في سورة النساء (¬6).

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:41-44/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:41-44/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:41-44/r1.claim: Joseph predicts that one companion will serve his master wine and the other will be crucified and eaten by birds; whether or not the dreams were genuine, the interpretation will happen.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:41-44/r1.anchor: يعني: سيقع بكما ما عبرت لكما

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:39/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:39/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:39/r1.claim: Ibn Ashur reports that Egyptians of the time had about thirty gods representing natural forces or stars.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:39/r1.anchor: Rivayete göre o dönemde Mısırlılar’ın otuz dolayında tanrıları vardı; bunlar farklı tabiat kuvvetlerini veya bazı yıldızları temsil ediyorlardı (İbn Âşûr, XII, 276)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:39/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:39/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:39/r3.claim: Joseph interprets one prisoner’s dream as his return to serving his master and serving wine, and the other’s as crucifixion with birds pecking his head.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:39/r3.anchor: birinin daha önce olduğu gibi efendisinin hizmetine gireceğini ve ona şarap sunacağını; diğerinin ise asılacağını, kafasını kuşların didikleyeceğini söylemiştir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Prophets seize opportunities to invite people to God's message; Joseph preached monotheism before interpreting the prisoners' dreams.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: he first delivered the message of monotheism to them and after that intepreted their dream for them.

FARRA:v2p45#2/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p45#2/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p45#2/r3.claim: It is reported that after Joseph interpreted the dreams and told one prisoner he would be crucified, the two denied having seen dreams; Joseph said the matter they asked about was settled.
FARRA:v2p45#2/r3.anchor:
ذكروا أنه لما عبر لهما الرؤيا فقال للآخر:
تصلب رجعا عن الرؤيا

THALABI:v5p223/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p223/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p223/r7.claim: The cupbearer’s three grape clusters mean three days in prison before he is restored to serving wine.
THALABI:v5p223/r7.anchor: أما أحدكما وهو الساقي، فيسقي ربه سيده يعني الملك خمرا

THALABI:v5p223/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p223/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p223/r8.claim: The baker’s three baskets mean three days before he is crucified on the fourth, leaving birds to eat his head.
THALABI:v5p223/r8.anchor: وأما الآخر فيصلب وأما السلال الثلاث التي رآها فإنها ثلاثة أيام

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r1.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r1.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r1.claim: The subjunctive after this fa is licensed by an implicit أن; it cannot be made explicit, just as the omitted element in لا يكون cannot be stated.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r1.anchor: الفاء إلا بإضمار أن ولا يجوز إظهار أن

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r2.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r2.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r2.claim: لم آتك is treated as equivalent to لم يكن إتيان, a noun-like construction that supplies the meaning for the following fa clause.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r2.anchor: بمنزلة لفظهم بلم يكن إتيان لأن المعنى واحد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r3.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r3.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r3.claim: ما تأتيني فتحدثني can mean that if you came you would speak, or that you never come without not speaking; it can also coordinate both negatives.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r3.anchor: ما تأتيني فكيف تحدثني أي لو أتيتني لحدثتني

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r4.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r4.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r4.claim: The accusative after fa is exemplified by لا يقضى عليهم فيموتوا, where the second verb is subjunctive.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r5.claim: Raising after fa is exemplified by the verse where they will not speak or be permitted to offer excuses; the raised verb follows the clause's syntactic position.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r5.anchor: @QB@ هذا يوم لا ينطقون ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r6.claim: A raised verb after fa may instead begin an independent predicate, equivalent to فأنت تحدثنا; Sībawayh gives a poetic parallel.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r6.anchor: كأنك قلت فأنت تحدثنا ومثل ~~ذلك قول بعض الحارثيين

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r7.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r7.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r7.claim: With ما أتيتنا فتحدثنا, the subjunctive is preferred to keep the clauses unified; raising can instead coordinate with the prior clause's syntactic position.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r7.anchor: وإنما اختير النصب لأن الوجه ههنا وحد الكلام

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r8.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r8.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r8.claim: ما تأتينا فتكلم إلا بالجميل has an implied أن and means that you would speak only well if you came; raising is also possible as coordination.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r8.anchor: المعنى أنك لو تأتنا إلا تكلمت بجميل ونصبه على إضمار أن

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r9.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r9.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r9.claim: The Farazdaq line وما قام منا قائم في ندينا فينطق إلا بالتي هي أعرف is another example of the subjunctive after fa.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r9.anchor: ما قام منا قائم في ندينا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r10.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r10.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r10.claim: In لا تأتينا فتحدثنا إلا ازددنا فيك رغبة, the subjunctive has the same construction as the earlier negative example; a line by al-Laʿīn illustrates it.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالفاء)#475/r10.anchor: فتحدثنا إلا ازددنا فيك رغبة فالنصب

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايضافإلىالأفعالمنالأسما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايضافإلىالأفعالمنالأسما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايضافإلىالأفعالمنالأسما.claim: Time nouns may be followed by a verbal clause, as in هذا يوم يقوم زيد; this is common in temporal expressions, where verbs can also function as modifiers.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايضافإلىالأفعالمنالأسما.anchor: يضاف إليها أسماء الدهر وذلك قولك هذا يوم يقوم زيد وآتيك يوم يقول ذاك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايضافإلىالأفعالمنالأسما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايضافإلىالأفعالمنالأسما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايضافإلىالأفعالمنالأسما.claim: Sībawayh cites two Qur'anic temporal clauses as examples of time nouns governing verbs.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايضافإلىالأفعالمنالأسما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايضافإلىالأفعالمنالأسما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايضافإلىالأفعالمنالأسما.claim: The same verbal addition occurs after منذ and مذ, as in منذ كان عندي and مذ جاءني.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايضافإلىالأفعالمنالأسما.anchor: ما رأيته منذ كان عندي ومذ جاءني

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايضافإلىالأفعالمنالأسما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايضافإلىالأفعالمنالأسما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايضافإلىالأفعالمنالأسما.claim: In بذي تسلم, ذو is attached to a verb and means the matter of your safety; Sībawayh says this is the only other such addition.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايضافإلىالأفعالمنالأسما.anchor: المعنى لا أفعل بسلامتك وذو مضافة إلى الفعل كإضافة ما قبله

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايضافإلىالأفعالمنالأسما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايضافإلىالأفعالمنالأسما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايضافإلىالأفعالمنالأسما.claim: The verb تقول may take two accusative complements in أتقول زيدا منطلقا, by analogy with تظن.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايضافإلىالأفعالمنالأسما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايضافإلىالأفعالمنالأسما.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايضافإلىالأفعالمنالأسما.claim: Past time expressions can be added to verbs or to a subject-predicate clause because they mean إذ; future time expressions only take verbs because they mean إذا.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايضافإلىالأفعالمنالأسما.anchor: لأنه في معنى إذ فأضيف إلى

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايضافإلىالأفعالمنالأسما.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايضافإلىالأفعالمنالأسما.speaker: يونس
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايضافإلىالأفعالمنالأسما.claim: Yunus reports from the Arabs that يكون هذا يوم زيد أمير is wrong: a future time expression cannot be followed by the nominal clause زيد أمير.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r1.claim: The root of قضى is حتم, to determine or make binding; in 39:42 death was decreed for the soul.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r1.anchor: أصل قضى: حتم، كقول الله عز وجل

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r2.claim: In 17:23 قضى means commanded: God made the command to worship Him alone binding.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r2.anchor: وقضى ربك ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r3.claim: In 17:4 قضينا means informed, since God's report that Israel would corrupt in the land was made certain.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r3.anchor: وقضينا إلى بني إسرائيل في الكتاب

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r4.claim: In 41:12 فقضاهن means He fashioned the seven heavens.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r5.claim: In 20:72 and 10:71, قضى means do or carry out what one intends.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r6.claim: Abū Dhuʾayb's قضاهما means made or fashioned the two coats of mail, by David or Tubbaʿ.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r6.anchor: وعليهما مسرودتان قضاهما ... داود أو صنع السوابغ تبع

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r7.claim: A poem about ʿUmar uses قضيت for doing and completing affairs.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r7.anchor: قضيت أمورا ثم غادرت بعدها ... بوائج في أكمامها لم تفتق

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r8.claim: A judge is called قاض because he settles and cuts off disputes; قضي قضاؤك and قد قضى for a dead person mean that the matter or life is finished.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r8.anchor: ومنه قيل للحاكم: قاض، لأنه يقطع على الناس الأمور ويحتم.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r9.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r9.claim: These senses branch from one underlying sense of determination and completion.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p247/r9.anchor: وهذه كلها فروع ترجع إلى أصل واحد.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r1.claim: Moses' signs—splitting the sea, the hand, the staff, and water from the rock—fit an age associated with sorcery.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r1.anchor: فكان لموسى فلق البحر، واليد، والعصا، وتفجر الحجر في التيه بالماء الرواء، إلى سائر أعلامه زمن السحر.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r2.claim: Jesus' raising the dead, making birds from clay, and healing the blind and lepers fit an age associated with medicine.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r2.anchor: وكان لعيسى إحياء الموتى، وخلق الطير من الطين، وإبراء الأكمه والأبرص، إلى سائر أعلامه زمن الطب.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r3.claim: Muhammad's chief sign is the Qur'an, beyond the capacity of humans and jinn to imitate, suited to the age of eloquence and البيان.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r3.anchor: وكان لمحمد صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم، الكتاب الذي لو اجتمعت الإنس والجن على أن يأتوا بمثله، لم يأتوا به

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r4.claim: Arab orators vary length, repetition, concealment, clarity, allusion, and euphemism to suit the occasion and their listeners.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r4.anchor: فالخطيب من العرب، إذا ارتجل كلاما في نكاح، أو حمالة، أو تحضيض، أو صلح، أو ما أشبه ذلك- لم يأت به من واد واحد

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r5.claim: A speech's manner depends on the situation, the occasion's scale, the size of the audience, and the dignity of the setting.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r5.anchor: وتكون عنايته بالكلام على حسب الحال، وقدر الحفل، وكثرة الحشد، وجلالة المقام.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r6.claim: A mix of polished and rough speech lets a lesser part point to a fuller one; making everything uniformly polished would drain its beauty.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r6.anchor: ثم لا يأتي بالكلام كله، مهذبا كل التهذيب، ومصفى كل التصفية، بل تجده يمزج ويشوب

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r7.claim: He illustrates variety with a meteor or torch, paired stars whose light diminishes, and a necklace mixing several precious materials.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r7.anchor: ومثل ذلك الشهاب من القبس نبرزه للشعاع، والكوكبان يقترنان، فينقص النوران، والسخاب ينظم بالياقوت والمرجان والعقيق والعقيان

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r8.claim: Arabic uses twenty-eight letters, while other languages fall short; apparent extra sounds are intermediate articulations between Arabic phonemes.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r8.anchor: وألفاظ العرب مبنية على ثمانية وعشرين حرفا، وهي أقصى طوق اللسان. وألفاظ جميع الأمم قاصرة عن ثمانية وعشرين

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r9.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r9.claim: Case endings adorn Arabic and can distinguish otherwise ambiguous meanings, including subject from object when either could fill the same syntactic position.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p17/r9.anchor: ولها الإعراب الذي جعله الله وشيا لكلامها، وحلية لنظامها، وفارقا في بعض الأحوال بين الكلامين المتكافئين، والمعنيين المختلفين

NASHR:v2p295/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p295/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p295/r4.claim: All agree on kasra in the prison at 12:36, both “companions of prison” verses, and 12:42: it means the place of confinement, not the verbal noun; Yaʿqūb's fatḥa at 12:33 distinguishes the noun from the verbal noun.
NASHR:v2p295/r4.anchor: ودخل معه السجن فتيان، وياصاحبي السجن للموضعين

NASHR:v2p136/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p136/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p136/r1.claim: The author says the sound position is to limit hāʾ al-sakt to readings explicitly permitted by Arabic authorities; most do not affirm it from Yaʿqub in this section.
NASHR:v2p136/r1.anchor: والصواب تقييده عند من أجازه كما نص عليه علماء العربية، والجمهور على عدم إثبات الهاء عن يعقوب

NASHR:v2p136/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p136/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p136/r2.claim: For the four special forms ويلتى، وأسفى، ويا حسرتى, and the adverb ثم, Ruways alone is disputed: Ibn Mihran and al-Kanz report hāʾ, while other transmitters omit it; al-Dani affirms it in ثم for Yaʿqub overall.
NASHR:v2p136/r2.anchor: فهي أربع (ويلتى، وأسفى، ويا حسرتى، وثم الظرف) فاختلف فيها عن رويس

NASHR:v2p136/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p136/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p136/r3.claim: Both forms for Ruways are sound; the author says he has read and adopts both.
NASHR:v2p136/r3.anchor: والوجهان صحيحان عن رويس قرأت بهما، وبهما آخذ

NASHR:v2p136/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p136/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p136/r4.claim: Al-Dani alone reports hāʾ in هلم for Yaʿqub; Ibn Mihran alone reports it in إياي and by analogy مثواي، محياي، أبي، and أخي, which requires an open yāʾ and is not Yaʿqub's reading.
NASHR:v2p136/r4.anchor: وانفرد الداني عن يعقوب بالهاء في هلم، وانفرد ابن مهران بالهاء في إياي

NASHR:v2p136/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p136/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p136/r5.claim: A report from Abu al-Hasan ibn Abi Bakr gives hāʾ only in the verb تستفتيان, but it opposes the other transmitters and is weak.
NASHR:v2p136/r5.anchor: وروي عن أبي الحسن بن أبي بكر المذكور تستفتيان بالهاء من الأفعال خاصة فخالف في ذلك سائر الرواة مع ضعفه

NASHR:v2p136/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p136/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p136/r6.claim: Arabic scholars permit hāʾ al-sakt in these and similar forms both by attested usage and by analogy.
NASHR:v2p136/r6.anchor: وهاء السكت في هذا كله وما أشبهه جائزة عند علماء العربية سماعا وقياسا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r1.claim: Exegetes have differed over whether taʾwil is identical to tafsir, narrower, or distinct from it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r1.anchor: وقد جرت عادة المفسرين بالخوض في بيان معنى التأويل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r2.speaker: ثعلب وابن الأعرابي وأبو عبيدة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r2.claim: Thalab, Ibn al-Arabi, and Abu Ubayda equate taʾwil with tafsir; this also appears to be al-Raghib's view.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r2.anchor: ذهب ثعلب وابن الأعرابي وأبو عبيدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r3.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r3.claim: Another view assigns tafsir to the apparent meaning and taʾwil to ambiguous passages.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r3.anchor: ومنهم من جعل التفسير للمعنى الظاهر والتأويل للمتشابه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r4.speaker: بعض الأصوليين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r4.claim: A Usuli definition treats taʾwil as moving a word from its apparent sense to another possible sense on the basis of evidence; extracting a bird from an egg is tafsir, while extracting a believer from an unbeliever is taʾwil.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r4.anchor: التأويل صرف اللفظ عن ظاهر معناه إلى معنى آخر محتمل لدليل فيكون هنا بالمعنى الأصولي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r5.claim: These are terminological conventions, but language and transmitted usage support the first view: taʾwil returns a statement to its intended meaning, like tafsir, especially in detailed explanation of a subtle meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r5.anchor: إلا أن اللغة والآثار تشهد للقول الأول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r6.speaker: الأعشى
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r6.claim: Al-Asha's line uses taʾwil for the gradual unfolding of love, like a young spring camel growing until it has a companion; Abu Ubayda glosses the image this way.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r6.anchor: على أنها كانت تأول حبها تأول ربعي السقاب فأصحبا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r7.claim: In the Quranic phrase about people awaiting its taʾwil, the word means the clarification that was intended.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r7.anchor: أي ينتظرون إلا بيانه الذي هو المراد منه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r8.claim: The Prophet prayed for Ibn Abbas to be given understanding of religion and taught taʾwil, meaning comprehension of the Quran's meanings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r8.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم في دعائه لأبن عباس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r9.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r9.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet said the supplication of glorification, praise, lordship, and forgiveness while bowing, describing this as acting on the Quran.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r9.anchor: وفي حديث عائشة رضي الله عنها كان صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول في ركوعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r10.claim: Aisha's phrase yataʾawwal al-Quran explicitly means that the Prophet acted on the verse's apparent meaning, not that he read it as signaling the approaching end of his mission.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r10.anchor: صريح في أنه فسر الآية بالظاهر منها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r11.speaker: عمر وابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r11.claim: Umar and Ibn Abbas understood the cited Quranic passage as indicating that the prophetic mission was nearing its end and the Prophet's departure was approaching.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p16/r11.anchor: الذي فهمه منها عمر وابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43/r1.speaker: فريق من العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43/r1.claim: One group identifies the seven aḥruf with words for a single meaning expressible in seven or fewer ways, including synonyms, dialect forms, and words with multiple readings; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this weak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43/r1.anchor: فذهب فريق من العلماء إلى أن تلك الحروف السبعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43/r2.speaker: ابن شهاب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43/r2.claim: Ibn Shihāb says he heard that the seven aḥruf concern one matter expressed in different ways without disagreement over lawful or forbidden matters; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls the statement possible but ambiguous.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43/r2.anchor: قال ابن شهاب في كتاب مسلم: «بلغني أن تلك السبعة الأحرف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43/r3.speaker: فريق من العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43/r3.claim: Another group takes the seven aḥruf as Quranic subject categories: command, prohibition, promise, threat, stories, disputation, and parables.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43/r3.anchor: وقال فريق من العلماء: «إن المراد بالسبعة الأحرف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects that category-based view because these subjects are not called aḥruf and consensus excludes changing legal rulings or those meanings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43/r4.anchor: وهذا أيضا ضعيف، لأن هذه لا تسمى أحرفا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43/r5.speaker: صاحب الدلائل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43/r5.claim: A reported scheme groups reading differences into seven kinds: vowel changes without meaning change; syntax or letters changing meaning; form changes preserving meaning; changes to both; word order; and addition or omission.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43/r5.anchor: وحكى صاحب الدلائل عن بعض العلماء، وقد حكى نحوه القاضي أبو بكر بن الطيب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43/r6.claim: Al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr ibn al-Ṭayyib cites a prophetic report describing seven doors and categories including command, prohibition, lawful and forbidden matters, clear and ambiguous verses, and parables.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p43/r6.anchor: وذكر القاضي أبو بكر بن الطيب في معنى هذه السبعة الأحرف حديثا عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v1p28/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p28/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v1p28/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet kept asking Gabriel for additional recitation modes after first receiving one, until they reached seven.
TAB-FULL:v1p28/r1.anchor: أن ابن عباس، حدثه: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، قال: «أقرأني جبريل على حرف

TAB-FULL:v1p28/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p28/r2.speaker: ابن شهاب
TAB-FULL:v1p28/r2.claim: Ibn Shihab says the seven ahruf concern a single matter whose forms do not differ over what is lawful or forbidden.
TAB-FULL:v1p28/r2.anchor: قال ابن شهاب: بلغني أن تلك السبعة الأحرف إنما هي في الأمر الذي يكون واحدا

TAB-FULL:v1p28/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p28/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v1p28/r3.claim: Umm Ayyub reports the Prophet's teaching that the Quran was revealed in seven ahruf and whichever form one recites is correct; the source repeats it with variant wording.
TAB-FULL:v1p28/r3.anchor: أخبره أبوه، أن أم أيوب أخبرته أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «أنزل القرآن على سبعة أحرف، أيها قرأت أصبت»

TAB-FULL:v1p28/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p28/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v1p28/r4.claim: Sulayman ibn Surad reports a prophetic account in which two angels offer one mode of recitation, and one keeps granting increases until seven.
TAB-FULL:v1p28/r4.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق، عن سليمان بن صرد، يرفعه، قال: " أتاني ملكان فقال أحدهما: اقرأ. قال: على كم؟ قال: على حرف

BURHAN:v1p468#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r1.speaker: الحليمي
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r1.claim: Al-Hulaymi counts avoiding the mixing of one surah with another among the etiquettes of recitation.
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r1.anchor: عد الحليمى من الآداب ترك خلط سورة بسورة

BURHAN:v1p468#2/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r2.speaker: البيهقي
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r2.claim: Al-Bayhaqi says the Qur’an’s arrangement came through the Prophet from Gabriel, so readers should follow the transmitted, agreed order.
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r2.anchor: قال البيهقى وأحسن ما يحتج به أن يقال إن هذا التأليف لكتاب الله مأخوذ من جهة النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم وأخذه عن جبريل

BURHAN:v1p468#2/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r3.speaker: ابن سيرين
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r3.claim: Ibn Sirin says God’s arrangement is better than people’s arrangement.
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r3.anchor: وقد قال ابن سيرين تأليف الله خير من تأليفكم

BURHAN:v1p468#2/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r4.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r4.claim: Qadi Abu Bakr transmits consensus against reciting one verse from each of several surahs in alternation.
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r4.anchor: ونقل القاضى أبو بكر الإجماع على عدم جواز قراءة آية آية من كل سورة

BURHAN:v1p468#2/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r5.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra says the Prophet heard Abu Bakr reciting softly, Umar loudly, and Bilal mixing passages from different surahs; he said they were all correct.
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r5.anchor: من حديث أبى هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مر بأبى بكر وهو يقرأ

BURHAN:v1p468#2/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r6.speaker: أبو عبيد
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r6.claim: Abu Ubayd’s version adds that Bilal was told to read a surah in its order, or to carry it through when reciting it.
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r6.anchor: وفى رواية لأبى عبيد فى فضائل القرآن قال بلال أخلط الطيب بالطيب فقال اقرأ السورة على وجهها أو قال على نحوها

BURHAN:v1p468#2/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r7.speaker: خالد بن الوليد
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r7.claim: Khalid ibn al-Walid once led prayer using passages from several surahs, then explained that jihad had kept him from learning the Qur’an.
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r7.anchor: وروى عن خالد بن الوليد أنه أم الناس فقرأ من سور شتى ثم التفت إلى الناس حين انصرف فقال شغلنى الجهاد عن تعلم القرآن

BURHAN:v1p468#2/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r8.speaker: أبو عبيد
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r8.claim: Abu Ubayd initially says the practice is disliked, citing the Prophet’s apparent disapproval of Bilal, Khalid’s apology, and Ibn Sirin’s dislike; he also notes a stronger report in which the Prophet says all the recitations are good.
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r8.anchor: ثم قال أبو عبيد الأمر عندنا على الكراهة فى قراءة القراء هذه الآيات المختلفة كما أنكر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على بلال

BURHAN:v1p468#2/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r9.speaker: أبو عبيد
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r9.claim: Abu Ubayd judges the version “all of that is good” more reliable and more consonant with the transmission of scholars.
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r9.anchor: ثم قال إن بعضهم روى حديث بلال وفيه فقال النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم كل ذلك حسن وهو أثبت وأشبه بنقل العلماء

BURHAN:v1p468#2/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r10.speaker: الحكيم الترمذي
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r10.claim: Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi compares Bilal to a bee that eats sweet and sour fruit yet produces healing, unlike birds that select only what tastes sweet.
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r10.anchor: ورواه الحكيم الترمذى فى نوادر الأصول وزاد مثل بلال كمثل نحلة غدت تأكل من الحلو والمر ثم يصير حلوا كله

BURHAN:v1p468#2/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r11.speaker: الحكيم الترمذي
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r11.claim: Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi says Bilal sought mercy verses and descriptions of Paradise, but the Prophet directed him to the revealed surah order: God mixed themes to meet people’s needs and keep hearts from weariness.
BURHAN:v1p468#2/r11.anchor: فبلال رضى الله عنه كان يقصد آيات الرحمة وصفات الجنة فأمره أن يقرأ السورة على نحوها كما جاءت ممتزجة كما أنزل الله تعالى

BURHAN:v3p143/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p143/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p143/r5.claim: In the passive “the matter about which you inquire has been decreed,” the agent is omitted to magnify the one who decreed it.
BURHAN:v3p143/r5.anchor: إذ كان الذي قضاه عظيم القدر

BURHAN:v1p211/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p211/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURHAN:v1p211/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Gabriel first recited one mode to the Prophet, who requested additional modes until seven were granted.
BURHAN:v1p211/r1.anchor: من حديث ابن عباس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أقرأنى جبريل على حرف فراجعته ثم لم أزل أستزيده

BURHAN:v1p211/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p211/r2.speaker: ابن شهاب
BURHAN:v1p211/r2.claim: Ibn Shihab says the seven modes concern a single matter whose ruling does not differ in what is lawful or forbidden.
BURHAN:v1p211/r2.anchor: قال ابن شهاب بلغني أن تلك السبعة إنما هى فى الأمر الذى يكون واحدا لا يختلف فى حلال ولا حرام

BURHAN:v1p211/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p211/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURHAN:v1p211/r3.claim: After hearing Hisham recite al-Furqan differently, the Prophet affirmed both Hisham's and Umar's recitations as revealed and allowed reciting what is easy.
BURHAN:v1p211/r3.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أرسله اقرأ فقرأ القراءة التى سمعته يقرأ فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هكذا أنزلت

BURHAN:v1p211/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p211/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURHAN:v1p211/r4.claim: Ubayy reports that the Prophet requested successive easings from one mode to two and then seven, and Ubayy chose forgiveness for the community while reserving his final request for Judgment Day.
BURHAN:v1p211/r4.anchor: وأخرج مسلم نحوه عن أبى بن كعب وفيه فقال النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم فإنى أرسل إلى أن اقرأ القرآن على حرف

BURHAN:v1p211/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p211/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURHAN:v1p211/r5.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra says the seven modes allow ease, but one must not end a mention of mercy with punishment or punishment with mercy.
BURHAN:v1p211/r5.anchor: عن أبى هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إن هذا القرآن أنزل على سبعة أحرف فاقرءوا ولا حرج
